description: We are X Astronomy Team, an Iraqi-founded team passionate about astronomy, space exploration, and science. Our goal is to bring together motivated people who want to learn, build, and solve real scientific and space-related challenges using creativity, research, technology, and teamwork.
summary:
We made an online service where you can give any coordinates on planet earth and be able to compare them with different terrain on the Moon and on Mars (such as Martian dust plains or the Moon’s frozen polar craters).
We put an emphasis on making the site as beginner friendly to use as possible. The whole experience is built to feel like a journey. Choose Mars and the screen warms to rust, choose the Moon and it cools to pale grey to match. And we don’t just show numbers. The site turns the raw measurements into plain sentences so the result can be understood without a science background, and wherever data is missing for a location, we say so openly too.
details:
Earth to Space finds the places on Earth that most closely resemble the Moon or Mars, and explains why.

Scientists and space agencies rely on teresstrial analog places on Earth to test rovers, rehearse missions and study geology they cannot reach. Choosing those sites is slow, specialist work. Earth to Space turns it into a question anyone can ask in a few seconds.

You begin by choosing a destination then the kind of terrain you want to match. You then search for a place on Earth by name, or enter coordinates directly. Our analysis service measures five environmental factors at that point: aridity and soil moisture, elevation and slope, geology and surface material, ice and water indicators, and temperature. Each is scored against the chosen profile and weighted by how much it matters to that mission (ice weighs heavily for a polar crater and lightly for a dusty plain) producing a single match percentage.

The result is shown as a radar chart comparing the location against a perfect match, alongside plain-language explanations built from the real measurements: “12 mm of rain a year against 1,800 mm of potential evaporation.” Where data is unavailable for a location, we say so openly and redistribute the weighting, rather than quietly scoring it zero.

The main feature that makes our project special is that you firstly get to choose the type of terrain on Mars or the Moon to compare with so it's not a One-size-fits-all approach since matching Martian dust plains for rover mobility demands different ground than matching the Moon’s permanently shadowed polar craters where water ice may survive. And secondly the different terrain you choose on Mars or the Moon changes the importance of different variables in the calculations.

As for the technical details:
Backend: Python with FastAPI, serving a point-query API that scores any coordinate against a chosen mission profile. Data is stored in Supabase. Deployed on Render.

Frontend: Built entirely from HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no frameworks or libraries. Every element, including the radar chart, the icons and the interface illustrations, is written by us as SVG.

The result is small, fast, runs on any web server, and is fully understood by our own team rather than assembled from parts we could not explain.
